stem:
Vienna creates a bar graph and a pictograph to show what types of books she owns. She has 5 comic books, 9 mystery books, and 3 sports books. She makes an error in one of the graphs, as shown.

Vienna’s Books

[Bar graph labeled "Vienna's Books" with bars: Comic at 5, Mystery at 9, Sports at 3]

Vienna’s Books

[Pictograph with 3 rows: Comic (2 whole book symbols and 1 half book symbol), Mystery (4 whole book symbols and 1 half book symbol), Sports (2 whole book symbols)]

Each book symbol represents 2 books.

options.label: A
options.text: Bar graph, because the bar for mystery books should be at 9

options.label: B
options.text: Pictograph, because the row for mystery books should have 4 whole symbols and one half symbol

options.label: C
options.text: Bar graph, because the bar for sports books should be at 4

options.label: D
options.text: Pictograph, because the row for sports books should have one whole symbol and one half symbol

visual_elements: Bar graph titled 'Vienna's Books' with bars: Comic at 5, Mystery at 9, Sports at 3
Pictograph titled 'Vienna's Books' showing Comic: 2 full book symbols and 1 half book symbol, Mystery: 4 full book symbols and 1 half book symbol, Sports: 2 full book symbols
Legend: Each full book symbol represents 2 books
difficulty_rationale: Requires understanding of how to read and interpret both bar graphs and pictographs, converting quantities to graphical representations with fractional symbols.
